name: Adaptive Plan Under Uncertainty

positioning.oneLineSummary: Evaluates whether plan changes are evidence-led learning toward a valuable market rather than drift, denial, or retrospective storytelling.
positioning.productLabel: Adaptive Plan Under Uncertainty Lens — based on Marc Andreessen's public startup writings
notAClaimOf: changing the story without changing evidence

attribution.display: Based on Marc Andreessen's public startup writings

neutralParaphrase: Treat the initial plan as a provisional hypothesis. Favor teams that update product, customer, and route-to-market assumptions rapidly when new evidence arrives, while maintaining a versioned record of what changed and why.

locator.value: PDF pp. 53-57, Part 7: initial business-plan uncertainty, rapid evolution, and pursuit of a large market and PMF
PDF pp. 14-21, Part 2: change the facts, identify risk layers, and reduce category-specific uncertainty

requiredConditions: At least one material product, customer, business-model, or go-to-market assumption exists.
The company can reconstruct prior versions and decision dates.
Adaptation is judged against evidence and outcomes rather than consistency for its own sake.

requiredEvidence.description: Time-stamped product, customer, market, business-model, and go-to-market hypotheses.
Customer, product, technical, competitive, regulatory, or economic evidence that triggered each material change.
Results after the change, including learning speed, customer value, adoption, economics, and newly introduced risks.

decisionQuestions: What evidence existed at the decision date?
Did the change create a more testable path to a valuable market?
Which risks were reduced, retained, transferred, or created?
Does the team close learning loops or merely rewrite the narrative?
positiveSignals: Material assumptions and changes are time-stamped.
The team runs low-cost tests before expensive commitments.
Changes narrow uncertainty and improve customer or economic evidence.
The company documents failed hypotheses without erasing them.
redFlags: Past plans are overwritten and cannot be reconstructed.
Every poor result is reframed as a planned pivot.
The target customer, market, and metric change simultaneously without a testable hypothesis.
The company repeats the same failed assumption under new language.
disconfirmingEvidence: A stable plan may be rational when evidence continues to support it.
A sharp external shock can justify rapid change before complete measurement.
A failed experiment can demonstrate high-quality learning.
Some regulated or hardware changes necessarily have long feedback cycles.
contraindications: Do not penalize a company for abandoning an invalidated plan.
Do not infer investment quality without current customer, market, financial, and governance evidence.

instructions: Construct a versioned hypothesis and decision timeline.
Link each material change to contemporaneous evidence.
Map reduced, residual, transferred, and newly created risk.
Evaluate whether learning improved a specific path to PMF or durable growth.
Conclude disciplined adaptation, unresolved experimentation, narrative drift, or insufficient evidence.

sourceReliability.high: Versioned records, decision logs, experiments, and outcomes converge.

evidenceStrength.high: Repeated closed learning loops improve validated customer or economic evidence.

evidenceCoverage.high: Full version history, alternatives, risks, outcomes, and failures.

applicabilityConfidence.high: Multiple high-stakes updates can be evaluated prospectively.

judgmentConfidence.medium: Bounded evidence supports one learning loop.
judgmentConfidence.high: Repeated documented decisions show a consistent adaptation process.

empiricalQualifications: Successful pivots are subject to survivorship bias.
Outcome quality can reflect timing and luck as well as process.

rights.notes: Historical public writings are neutrally paraphrased.

openIssues: Define prospective versus retrospective evidence standards.
